title: Adaptive probing with mixed key and non-key share counts
summary: Determine whether adaptive stateful masking can use 2t+1 key shares but only t+1 shares for every non-key variable.

formal_statement.body: For the source's randomized table-recomputation implementation of a full block cipher, let the adversary place at most $t$ probes in each execution and move probe positions adaptively between executions. Is perfect simulation security achievable with $2t+1$ shares for the persistent secret-key variables and $t+1$ shares for all non-key variables, including lookup-table inputs, outputs, encoding, decoding, and refresh state, for every masking order $t$? A complete result must either construct and prove this exact mixed-share interface secure or exhibit a compatible adaptive probing attack.

scope.domain: Adaptive and stateful probing security of higher-order masked lookup-table implementations in symmetric block ciphers
assumptions: The lookup-table countermeasure and randomized refresh operations are those defined by Coron's source construction
Persistent secret-key variables use 2t+1 randomized Boolean shares
All non-key and transient variables use t+1 shares
The adversary may place at most t probes in each execution and change probe locations adaptively between executions
Security is perfect simulation security in the full stateful probing model
parameters: number of executions and state transitions
scope.unresolved_remainder: TCHES 2018 proves t-SNI for the table-recomputation gadget and enables t+1 shares for that gadget, while CCS 2016 gives a robust stateful composition with 2t+2-share region boundaries. No inspected result proves or refutes the exact 2t+1 persistent-key and t+1 non-key interface under adaptive cross-execution probing.
